verdict.rationale: mise keeps its data in plain, open files that you own. Tool versions are recorded in a checked-in `mise.toml`, tasks can be standalone executable shell scripts, and it reads standard asdf `.tool-versions` and idiomatic version files. Leaving therefore needs no proprietary extraction, but the evidence shows no documented export, migrate-out or uninstall path. Missing for 10: a documented export/migration-out workflow (e.g. writing `.tool-versions` or other formats), documented uninstall/clean-leave guidance, and independent corroboration of portability when leaving.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: `mise use` installs Node.js 24 if needed and records the request in a new `mise.toml`
mise replaces them with one file that's checked in, so a fresh laptop is `git clone` and `mise bootstrap`.
You can also define tasks as standalone shell scripts. All you have to do is create an `executable` file in a specific directory like `mise-tasks`.
the ability to write tasks as actual bash script files rather than inside yml/json/toml strings
mise is also compatible with asdf `.tool-versions` files and with idiomatic version files like `.node-version` and `.ruby-version`.
